prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.76
  gal: 0.24
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax, and regulation
- Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 via a civil service recruitment freeze, removal of 235,000 bureaucratic posts, and cutting/abolishing 168 public bodies.
- Use £8bn of savings to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts in the first Budget; grow total public spending at 4% a year to 2011–12.
- Maintain the minimum wage; halve council tax bills for many pensioner households (up to £500, funded centrally).
- Link the basic state pension to earnings; retain Winter Fuel Payment, free TV licences (75+), and the one-off £200 council tax payment (that year).
- Create Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; encourage “opt-out” workplace pensions; use unclaimed financial assets to help those hit by failed schemes.
- Reduce business regulation via departmental regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, and ending “gold-plating” of EU rules.
- Keep Bank of England independence; retain the pound (no Euro).

Family policy and education
- Flexible maternity pay (over 6 or 9 months); up to £50/week childcare support per under‑5 for eligible working families, with simpler access and choice of formal/informal care; more workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore school discipline: heads/governors control admissions and expulsions; create Turnaround Schools; cut teacher paperwork.
- Simplify school funding so money follows the pupil; allow growth of good schools; 600,000 additional places in first term.
- Publish exam marks with grades; allow international qualifications; slim the National Curriculum and increase academic rigour.
- 300,000 vocational grants (£1,000 each) for 14–16-year-olds; two hours of after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools; safer school trips.
- Permit free places at independent schools where costs match state funding.
- Moratorium on closing special schools; reform further education funding and governance; scrap university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; support university endowments.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn a year over the Parliament (to ~£2,000 per head); cut central bureaucracy (abolish Strategic Health Authorities, reduce PCTs/quangos); scrap central targets.
- Greater local autonomy: empower professionals; bring back matrons with ward-closure powers; invest in infection control and single rooms.
- Patient/GP choice of providers; funding follows the patient; protect viable community hospitals.
- Partial NHS rebate (about half NHS cost) for self-funded operations to help reduce waiting lists.
- Social care partnership to avoid forced home sales; more respite/support for carers.
- Improve NHS dentistry access with new contracts and low monthly prepayment schemes.
- Health checks for non‑EU migrants staying over 12 months and for permanent settlement; STI public health campaign.

Crime, justice, and security
- Recruit 5,000 additional police officers per year; cut paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners; focus on neighbourhood policing.
- End early release; add 20,000 prison places; “honesty in sentencing.”
- Expand drug treatment, including 25,000 residential rehab places; reverse cannabis reclassification.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; strengthen counter‑terror capabilities.

Immigration and borders
- 24/7 port surveillance; restore embarkation controls; create a Border Control Police.
- Australian‑style points system for work permits.
- Set an annual overall migration limit, including a quota for UNHCR‑referred refugees; process asylum claims outside the UK; seek national control over asylum rules including changes to international/EU frameworks.

Governance and devolution
- Publish a delivery timetable; strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; reduce MPs by 20%; pursue a largely elected upper chamber.
- Abolish regional assemblies; return planning, housing, transport, and fire service powers to local authorities.
- “English votes for English laws”; Wales referendum on Assembly powers; uphold the consent principle in Northern Ireland.

Communities, transport, environment, and rural
- More local say on planning; stronger action on illegal traveller encampments; devolve arts/lottery funding.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Modernise roads; review all speed cameras; lengthen rail franchises.
- Protect Green Belt; prioritise brownfield development.
- Phase out HFCs; incentivise home energy efficiency; lower VED and grants for low‑emission cars; increase recycling; support renewables and efficiency for energy security.
- Honest food labelling; require Little Red Tractor in public procurement; further CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote on hunting ban.

Defence and foreign policy
- Increase front‑line defence by £2.7bn by 2007–08; support service families; preserve regiments; retain warships; keep NATO central.
- Support Iraq reconstruction and a Middle East peace based on Israeli security and a viable Palestinian state.
- EU: referendum on the Constitutional Treaty within six months; oppose Euro; seek reform of social/employment rules; repatriate fisheries control; support enlargement (including Turkey).
- Overseas aid: work toward 0.7% of national income by 2013; seek greater national control over aid spending.

Immediate actions (first month/day)
- Begin recruiting extra police; reinstate matrons; first Budget to cut waste and reduce taxes; empower head teachers to expel; initiate 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU referendum date.

TEXT_C:
This 2005 manifesto proposes changes across the economy, environment, welfare, public services, transport, democracy, and international policy.

Economy and taxation
- More progressive income tax bands (illustrative: 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and additional corporation tax bands (up to 40% on profits over £1.5m).
- Shift taxation from labour and consumption to resource use and pollution: abolish National Insurance, phase out VAT, introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes (including aviation fuel; levies on plastic bags).
- Pilot a Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies, support for small businesses; oppose joining the euro; seek reform of global trade rules.
- Job creation via renewable energy, low‑carbon transport, and zero‑waste industries; defend workplace rights and reduce working hours.
- Supplement GDP with well‑being metrics (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut CO2 by 20% (2010), 50% (2020), 85% (2030); develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic energy VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges; protect low‑use consumers.
- Reach 40% renewable energy by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; deploy solar, small‑scale wind, offshore wind/wave, and biogas.
- Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy demand 30% in 10 years; local “Smart Energy Councils” targeting 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- Decommission nuclear plants at end of life; end nuclear R&D support.

Welfare, housing, work and families
- Phase in a universal, non‑means‑tested Citizen’s Income; retain specialist benefits and initially retain housing benefit.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension, earnings‑linked, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support and increase child benefit in the first phase; end the Working Time Directive opt‑out; explore a 35‑hour week; expand early‑years centres.
- Boost affordable housing: let councils reinvest sale receipts, support self‑build co‑ops, apply LVT, and upgrade insulation/efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore a universal NHS free at point of use; end PPPs and resist service liberalisation.
- Abolish prescription charges; reintroduce free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Increase health funding to about 9% of GNP; consider a hypothecated NHS tax; redirect future defence savings to health.
- Increase education funding (pre‑school and post‑16), scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants, abolish SATs, and promote individual learning plans.

Transport
- Target a 10% road‑traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road building to public transport; re‑regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs via congestion charging/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish car tax discs; vary freight duty by size/axle/pollution; fund R&D in efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: oppose new runways, ban night flights, seek EU aviation fuel tax; tax domestic flight emissions; raise Air Passenger Duty; shift short‑haul to rail.

Environment, food, and animal welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration, reduce packaging, set recycled content standards, create a Zero Waste Agency; aim for 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
- Environmental Protection Commission; eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen chemicals regulation.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, and nanotechnology; oppose patents on natural resources.
- Animal welfare: extend hunting bans, replace vivisection, end live exports, ban battery eggs (including enriched), tighten broiler rules, ban fur imports.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local food chains; ban GM food.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies backing local markets, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes for farming and fishing.

Crime and justice
- Prevention through urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more caretakers; treat drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards and redirect funds to prevention.
- Strengthen community policing, accountability, and local stations; revive community wardens/keepers.
- Tighten gun laws: quantitative lethality threshold, broader prohibitions, treat deactivated guns as active for licensing, single rigorous licensing, ongoing expert review.
- Expand restorative justice; enhance responses to hate crimes, violence against women; support stronger disability rights.

Democracy and constitutional reform
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Devolve power to local and regional levels; introduce proportional representation for local and national elections.
- Enable local recall (40%) and referenda (20% trigger); empower local taxation via LVT.
- Fully elected upper chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; limit monarchy’s formal roles.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating EU reform to enhance democracy and sustainability.

International policy
- Ethical foreign policy: prioritise diplomacy, UN peacekeeping, and conflict prevention; withdraw troops from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers.
- Reduce defence spending to EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end arms export subsidies/credits; negotiate an Arms Trade Treaty; ban use of depleted uranium.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax; enable North–South carbon finance flows.
- Reform UN Security Council (end permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Overhaul global trade rules to permit localisation and sustainability, replacing or modifying WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade.
- Asylum/migration: uphold refugee rights, speed decisions, allow work/benefits, provide independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; review domestic asylum law; support improved EU standards.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.
